checks: Finite nets include every original occupied site and preserve enough affine-independent points in each positive-volume fiber. Sandwiching each approximating fiber between its own net hull and the old fiber gives simultaneous Hausdorff approximation and exact lattice projection.

The central site is full-dimensional by the positive barycentric-weight argument. Relative full dimension of the lifted hull allows a finite ambient halfspace description; vertical facets only restrict the projection and are redundant at the fixed sampled sites. The same nonvertical rows therefore represent every sampled fiber of the approximant.

Normalized maximum depth is continuous on the common bounded approximants by total variation of summed fiber volumes and the moving-mark slab estimate. The proof of this part of the accepted theorem applies before central-volume normalization and in lower base rank.

The allowed fiber-affine maps transform the common continuous normals by A inverse transpose, preserve the shared count and multiply every cap and total mass by the same determinant. The bounded normalization and simultaneous compactness give a positive-mass limit with central volume one. Shared-plane closure retains N and depth continuity proves attainment.

If there are null fibers, the compatible deletion theorem gives exact remaining lattice-complete projection and preserves all measured mass and maximal depth. In the all-positive case the shared coefficient chart gives actual nearby variations after rescaling.
